title: Positive local depth of finite intermediate restriction quotients
statement: Let $L$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $U$ an open subscheme, and $N$ a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent], finite on every affine open. Assume the restriction unit is injective on sections of every open, and every stalk $N_y$ outside $U$ is finite of depth at least two [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Fix an affine open $V$, put $R=\mathcal O_L(V)$, $M=N(V)$ and $P=(j_*(N|_U))(V)$, and write $a:M\to P$ for the unit. For any finitely generated $R$-submodule $S\subseteq P$ containing $a(M)$, put $K=\{s\in S:s\in a(M)\}$ and $Q=S/K$. For every prime ideal $p$ of $R$, the localization $Q_p$ is finite over $R_p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and has depth at least one. The zero localization is included, with infinite depth.

source.place: Tag 0AV8, proof: finite intermediate submodule and short exact sequence paragraphs; Tag 0E9I, proof via 0AVN; Tags 05AM, 00LL and 00LX

proof.text: On the Noetherian affine V, quasi-coherence identifies the source with the sheaf of M. The open immersion U intersect V into V is qcqs, and its pushforward is quasi-coherent with module P. The unit is injective by hypothesis and an isomorphism on U intersect V. By 0AVN boundary points are not weakly associated to P, hence are not associated (05AM). This is the affine setup of the proof of 0E9I. The affine stalk comparisons identify R_p with the local ring at the corresponding point and M_p with N at that point; they transport the boundary depth assumption and the unit map.

Associated primes of the submodule S are contained in those of P. Localizing the injective map M into S produces 0 -> M_p -> S_p -> Q_p -> 0. Over U the first map is an isomorphism, so Q_p is zero and has infinite depth. At boundary primes S_p, if nonzero, has depth at least one by 00LL since its maximal ideal is not associated. When M_p and Q_p are nonzero the quotient inequality in 00LX and depth(M_p) >= 2 imply depth(Q_p) >= 1. If M_p is zero, Q_p is isomorphic to S_p; if S_p or Q_p is zero, the quotient is zero. Thus every case has the claimed lower bound.

Finite generation of S gives finite generation of S/K, and its localization is finite over R_p. Together with the preceding depth inequality this gives the asserted existential witness for the finiteness instance.

    (hqc : N.IsQuasicoherent)
    (hsections : ∀ V : L.Opens, IsAffineOpen V →
      Module.Finite (L.presheaf.obj (op V)) (N.val.obj (op V)))

            (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) (X := L) N.val.presheaf y),
        letI := hfinite
        (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := L.presheaf.stalk y)
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) (X := L) N.val.presheaf y)) 
    (hinj : ∀ V : L.Opens,
      Function.Injective (((Modules.restrictAdjunction U.ι).unit.app N).app V))
    (V : L.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (S : Submodule (L.presheaf.obj (op V))
      (((Modules.pushforward U.ι).obj
        ((Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj N)).val.obj (op V)))
    (hS : S.FG)

    (p : Ideal (L.presheaf.obj (op V))) [p.IsPrime] :

      (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p
        (S ⧸ (LinearMap.range
          (((Modules.restrictAdjunction U.ι).unit.app N).val.app (op V)).hom).comap
            S.subtype)),
      letI := hfinite
      (1 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := Localization.AtPrime p)
